supporting_observations.claim: The reported PowerShell appearance at approximately 13:40 UTC falls within the 13:30–14:10 UTC endpoint winsec and Sysmon collection outage, so the supplied endpoint records do not verify what process ran then.

At 13:57 UTC, FILE-HD-01 initiated a TCP connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01 on port 135. The inventory says remote administration is only performed from WS-OHADDAD-01, making this connection noteworthy, but the record does not establish its purpose.

At 13:44 UTC, the workstation used the proxy to download about 38.8 MB from download.windowsupdate.com with a Windows Update Agent user agent, consistent with patch activity but not proof of who initiated it.

At 14:11 UTC, GoogleDriveFS.exe ran as maria.lopez, and the workstation connected to dl.google.com using a Google Update user agent. Google Drive is not among the approved services listed in the environment context.

Sysmon recorded svchost.exe accessing lsass.exe several times between 14:11 and 14:12 UTC. These records alone do not establish whether the access was malicious or explain the source process's purpose.
The conhost.exe process recorded at 14:12 UTC had csrss.exe as its parent; these records do not show that it was associated with PowerShell.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor coverage metadata reports a winsec and Sysmon collection outage on WS-MLOPEZ-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, covering the reported 13:40 event. Records immediately before and after that window include T024-00072 and T024-00276, but they cannot establish activity during the gap.

The available FILE-HD-01 connection records show a connection to the workstation on port 135 but do not identify the remote process or the activity carried over that connection (T024-00169, T024-00170).

The available endpoint process and proxy records show Google Drive running and contacting Google Update, but do not establish whether files were uploaded or what data, if any, was transferred (T024-00278, T024-00281).
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell launched on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at approximately 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its command line, parent process, user, and actions.
Whether the FILE-HD-01 connection to WS-MLOPEZ-01 was authorized or what activity it performed.
Whether the Windows Update transfer was initiated as part of scheduled IT patching.
Whether Google Drive was used for file storage or transfer, and whether any organizational data was uploaded.
What prompted the svchost.exe access to lsass.exe or whether it was benign.
Whether any of these events resulted in compromise or impact.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover WS-MLOPEZ-01 winsec and Sysmon logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including process creation, PowerShell logging, and process access details.
Identify the process and service responsible for the FILE-HD-01 to WS-MLOPEZ-01 port 135 connection and correlate it with FILE-HD-01 logs and any relevant approved job or administration records.
Check Google Drive installation and authorization status, and review available file-sync or proxy evidence for uploads or other data transfer.
Correlate the Windows Update activity with WS-OHADDAD-01 patching records and the organization's patch schedule.
